steps: Pascal’s Law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the liquid and to the walls of its container.
The pressure acts at right angles to the surfaces in contact with the liquid.
1. Hydraulic press: It is used to compress materials, such as cotton or scrap metal. A small force applied to the small piston produces a large force on the larger piston.
2. Hydraulic brakes: In vehicles, pressure applied to the brake pedal is transmitted through the brake fluid to the brakes at the wheels, slowing or stopping the vehicle.
3. Hydraulic lift: It is used to raise heavy vehicles in workshops. Pressure applied to a small piston is transmitted through the liquid and produces a large lifting force on a larger piston.
items.finalAnswer: Pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions; hydraulic presses, brakes and lifts are examples of its applications.

steps: Given: Altitude = 150 m, 500 m, 800 m, 1140 m, 1300 m and 1500 m; pressure = 99.5 kPa, 95.7 kPa, 92.4 kPa, 88.9 kPa, 87.2 kPa and 85.3 kPa, respectively.
Required: Air pressure at sea level (altitude = 0 m), in Pa.
Plot altitude on the x-axis and pressure on the y-axis; plot the given data points and draw a best-fit straight line.
Extend the line to altitude 0 m. From the graph, the pressure intercept is approximately 101 kPa.
Convert to SI units: 101 kPa = 101 × 10³ Pa.
Result: Air pressure at sea level ≈ 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa.
